correctness.rationale: Let N=n−2 and let the host have N+e zeros. Each target 0^a110^(N−a) needs two distinct host ones at zero levels in [a,a+e]; disjoint windows spaced e+1 apart give at least 2 ceil((N+1)/(e+1)) ones, and AM–GM gives the lower bound. For the proposed host with N+2g zeros, round the prefix and middle requirements up to multiples of g, forcing a positive multiple for the middle even when b=0. The second chosen zero level is at most a+b+2g=N+2g−c, so both the last available one and the required suffix are respected. g=ceil(sqrt(N/2)) gives the frozen upper inequality for every N≥1; the asymptotic follows. Independent exhaustive host enumeration for n=3 through 12 returned 5,7,9,10,12,14,15,17,18,20, and the construction was independently checked through n=160. The finite checks corroborate, not prove, the general bounds.
